beats.story: Back at my desk, I unlock my phone and stop the recording. Two new text notifications from my mom are waiting for me. MOM: There's a new cheat where they sneak drugs in your luggage and another guy kidnaps you! Don't travel. MOM: Also, Starbucks is a waste of money. I swipe them away unread, linking my headphones to press play. The dead static of an empty boardroom plays. I hit pause.
beats.story_cn: 回到座位，我解锁手机停止了录音。妈妈发来两条未读短信。老妈：现在有种骗局是往你行李里塞毒品，还有同伙绑架你！别出门旅游。老妈：还有，星巴克纯粹是浪费钱。我划掉通知没点开，戴上耳机按下播放键。空荡会议室的死寂静电噪音响起。我按了暂停。

beats.story: Anything could be in this recording. Yeah, Gregory will surely make me recoil minute one, but that's not what's tensing my butt cheeks. It's silly. It's literally Cliff's job to talk about me behind my back. I need to get a grip. It's this place -- that's it. As if to confirm my fears, footsteps tumble behind me as Larry and Joy pass by, matching mugs in hand and downturned mouths. They're discussing the quality of the duffel bag they each got as a fifteen-year appreciation gift from Supershops.
beats.story_cn: 录音里什么都有可能。当然，格雷戈里肯定让我开场一分钟就想遁地，但让我屁股发紧的还不是这事。真傻，克里夫的工作本来就是在背后议论我。我得冷静点。是这鬼地方——就为这个。仿佛印证我的恐惧，拉里和乔伊举着同款马克杯、耷拉着嘴从我身后走过。他们正讨论着“超级商店”十五年司龄纪念礼——每人一个行李袋的质量问题。

beats.story: I can't do it here. I can't hear something that'll make me want to dissolve into a pile of dust while Stu fiddles with the angle of his desk fan. But I can't wait until I'm safely at home either. I can't sit through another car ride with Cliff if he's sold me out. I slide my phone into my back pocket. I'm only too aware of myself and everyone I pass as I head toward the elevator, then keep going straight. The archive room at the end of the hall greets me like a dark cloak, the earthy cardboard scent beckoning me inside. The shelves are stacked so tightly with bulky file boxes they basically soundproof the room.
beats.story_cn: 我不能在这儿听。我不能边听可能让我当场灰飞烟灭的内容，边看斯图摆弄他办公桌小风扇的角度。但也不能等到安全回家再听。如果克里夫真把我卖了，我可受不了一路同车。我把手机塞进后裤袋。从走向电梯开始，我对自己和每个擦肩之人都变得过分警觉，随即径直走过电梯。走廊尽头的档案室像件黑色斗篷般迎接我，牛皮纸箱散发的沉闷气息引诱我步入。架子上密密麻麻堆满厚重的文件盒，几乎把房间隔成消音室。

beats.story: I've actually had a few decent cry breaks in here. Turning on the lights will surely draw the attention of a passerby, so I crouch in a corner and fully settle into the sensory deprivation of the dark room as I pop in my headphones and press play. I speed past the initial greetings, managing to stop when Gregory just has to say, "Let's get to the meat and potatoes then. What did you want to discuss?" Cliff lets out a labored breath and says, "Well, I've met with most of the seventh-floor employees so far, but the most pressing thing is the employee in mandatory stress training. I think some of the resentments with the company are beyond the parameters of what we're covering. The course isn't designed to address these kinds of underlying mental health issues, and it's not in my interest to set someone up for failure or inhibit their long-term success with Supershops." My heart drops into my stomach. Cliff had promised me he wouldn't say anything when I panicked in his office. And now he has to tell the worst fuck in the world about my issues.
beats.story_cn: 我其实在这儿哭过好几次，挑的都是还算得体的时机。开灯肯定会引来路过同事的目光，所以我蜷缩在角落，完全沉浸在黑暗带来的感官剥夺中，塞上耳机按下播放键。我快速跳过开头的寒暄，精准停在格雷戈里开口的瞬间：“那我们直奔主题吧。你想讨论什么？”克利夫沉重地呼出一口气说道：“嗯，目前我已经和七楼大部分员工谈过，但最紧迫的是那位必须参加压力培训的员工。我认为他对公司积怨的问题已经超出了课程涵盖范畴。这门课本就不是为了解决这类潜在心理健康问题而设计的，而且我也没兴趣给人挖坑断送他在‘超级卖场’的前程。”我的心脏直坠胃底。克利夫曾向我保证，当我在他办公室崩溃时，他绝不会透露半句。而现在他却不得不把我的事告诉全世界最混蛋的家伙。

beats.story: This is why I shouldn't have eaten his donuts or agreed to go out for milkshakes. I should never have agreed to be his carpool buddy. He's an HR guy deep in his soul. Gregory clears his throat. "Well, that sounds simple enough. Failing the course equals termination." My blood freezes. Cliff's voice comes back. "Actually, I want to propose that the company provide more mental health support." Gregory's laugh charges through my earbuds and grates against my bones.
beats.story_cn: 这就是为什么我不该吃他的甜甜圈，不该答应去喝奶昔。我压根不该同意和他拼车上班——他骨子里就是个HR。格雷戈里清了清嗓子：“嗯，听起来很简单。课程不合格即终止合同。”我的血液瞬间凝固。克利夫的声音再次传来：“实际上，我建议公司应提供更完善的心理健康支持。”格雷戈里的笑声刺穿我的耳机，像钝器刮过骨头。

beats.story: There's a moment of silence, filled only by my pounding heart. "I understand that position," Cliff finally says, voice soft as a baby's bum. "But this is a long-term employee we're talking about. If we ignore systemic issues and simply terminate, it can cause more costly problems. Big picture: I've seen this in many companies I've worked with. Supershops' policies have contributed to a culture of resentment and feelings of insecurity from within." "Insecurity is one of the most effective motivators for productivity. I'm running one of the largest retailers in the country." Gregory's laugh rips through me again, churning my stomach. "Between you and me, it's great when employees fail these last-chance courses.
beats.story_cn: 寂静中只听得见我擂鼓般的心跳。“我理解这个立场，”克里夫终于开口，声音柔得像婴儿屁股。“但我们谈论的是一位资深员工。若无视系统性问题而直接解雇，反而会引发代价更高的问题。往大了说——我在合作过的许多公司都见过这种情况。‘超级商店’的政策助长了怨恨文化，让员工内心充满不安。”“不安可是激发效率最管用的动力之一。我经营着全国最大的零售商之一。”格雷戈里的笑声再次撕裂空气，搅得我胃里翻江倒海。“说句掏心窝的，员工通不过这些最后机会课程，其实是好事。”

Well, if she ends up failing -- " Cliff's tone sharpens. "I find that very unlikely -- " "That Armin kid is another low-hanging fruit," Gregory interrupts.

I'd eat Gregory alive if he wasn't so disgusting. "Who exactly is the 'they' you're referring to?" Cliff's voice cuts sharper than I've ever heard.
